extra: First $0500 bytes of the mission payload.
Second destination for the mission payload, $3EF0 bytes.

comments.text: Twenty consecutive 64-byte sprite slots in VIC bank $4000. Each slot begins with 21 rows of three pixel bytes, and the last byte is outside the displayed height.
Four sprite slots after the first sixteen mission frames. The VIC slot positions relative to bank $4000 are $A0-$A3.

Four rows of four character codes per 16-byte tile. The map renderer resolves a tile ID through the resident screen-code pointer tables, then indexes this pattern with the character coordinates modulo four.
Tile dictionary slots for IDs $40-$7F in the mission 5 dictionary. Entries are 16 bytes apart.

Twenty-one zero-terminated screen-code lines, indexed by the ending row pointers at $F891/$F8B9. The lines name Random Access, Simon Pick, Ned Langman, Tiny Williams, Nick Pelling, Jacco and Daniel Marchant.
Line 21 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 9 and writes 26 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 22 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 14 and writes 13 character codes before the zero terminator.
Blank C64 credits row, referenced by line 23 of the scroll list.
Line 24 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 16 and writes 11 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 25 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 16 and writes 10 character codes before the zero terminator.
Blank C64 credits row, referenced by line 26 of the scroll list.
Line 27 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 17 and writes 8 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 28 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 16 and writes 11 character codes before the zero terminator.
Blank C64 credits row, referenced by line 29 of the scroll list.
Line 30 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 15 and writes 13 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 31 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 15 and writes 13 character codes before the zero terminator.
Blank C64 credits row, referenced by line 32 of the scroll list.
Line 33 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 16 and writes 11 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 34 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 16 and writes 12 character codes before the zero terminator.
Blank C64 credits row, referenced by line 35 of the scroll list.
Line 36 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 10 and writes 22 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 37 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 18 and writes 5 character codes before the zero terminator.
Blank C64 credits row, referenced by line 38 of the scroll list.
Line 39 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 7 and writes 27 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 40 of the C64 credits. The renderer starts at screen column 13 and writes 15 character codes before the zero terminator.
Zero bytes following the final credit string's terminator. The next range at $C9A0 is also zero.
Dictionary slots for tile IDs $9A–$AF. All sixteen character indices in each slot are zero. The renderer resolves these slots through the same resident pointer tables as the populated patterns.
Complete 256-glyph source for the $ADF7 scene. Each glyph occupies eight bytes. The masked wipe at $1E17 reads from this base with an eight-byte stride and writes the corresponding row at $4000.
Tile-indexed colour bytes. The initial playfield renderer at $17CD reads these in parallel with the tile character pointers and $1882 writes the chosen value to colour RAM.
Primary 256-character graphics source. The resident wipe routine at $1DC2 enables RAM under I/O and copies the selected pixel rows to the live character set at $4000.
Rows for character codes $80-$FF in the main stage's 256-glyph set. The masked copy selects them through the same eight-byte stride as the lower codes.
Alternate 256-character graphics source in RAM below the I/O window. The resident wipe routine chooses this source when $1902 is set, unless the alternate scene flag $ADF7 takes priority.
The upper half of the alternate stage's eight-byte character slots, read under CIA and expansion register addresses with I/O banked out.
Stage 1 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 1 tile grid from row 10, column 1. The grid has 64 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
Stage 1 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 1 attribute grid from row 10, column 1. The grid has 64 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
Stage 2 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 2 tile grid from row 10, column 1. The grid has 64 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
Stage 2 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 2 attribute grid from row 10, column 1. The grid has 64 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
Stage 3 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 3 tile grid from row 10, column 1. The grid has 64 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
Stage 3 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 3 attribute grid from row 7, column 36. The grid has 64 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
Stage 3 attribute grid from row 10, column 1. The grid has 64 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
Stage 4 grid, 20 entries per row and first 7 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 4 tile grid from row 8, column 1. The grid has 20 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
Sixteen loaded zero bytes after the stage-four tile grid, before the stage-four attribute grid starts.
Stage 4 grid, 20 entries per row and first 7 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 4 attribute grid from row 8, column 1. The grid has 20 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
Forty-eight loaded zero bytes after the final declared stage-four attribute row.
Sixteen 64-byte source slots that the bootstrap at $F7C8 transfers to $6440. The mirror routine generates further frames in live sprite storage from this copy.
Six 64-byte frames copied from $F440 to $6440 by the alternate sprite installer. It mirrors those frames into the following six slots at $65C0.

When $24 differs from 2, configures the two actor slots as type $0C, clears eight sprite-history Y entries and installs the alternate frames. Then calls the primary actor update, history update and secondary sprite setup.

Runs the final actor sequence while switching the VIC display mode on two raster boundaries relative to the actor's Y coordinate. After the actor state clears, clears both screen pages and colour RAM row by row, copies the text glyphs and calls the ending scroller.

Disables sprites, selects black background colours and patches the three row stores from the resident screen and colour row tables. Clears 21 rows of both screen pages and sets the corresponding colour RAM cells to one. Then copies a page of glyph rows from $5108 to $4008 and starts the text renderer at $FA76.
Indexed store of zero to the first screen page. The row address is patched at $F6D4 and $F6E0.
Low byte of the first screen row's store address, copied from $9450.
High byte of the first screen row's store address, copied from $9466.
Indexed store of zero to the second screen page for the same row and column.
Low byte of the second screen row's store address, copied from $9450.
High byte of the second screen row's store address, four pages above the first screen.
Indexed store of colour one to the current row in colour RAM.
Low byte of the colour row's store address, shared with the two screen rows.
High byte of the colour row's store address from $0AB6. The loop writes 40 cells per row, then copies the ending glyphs and begins drawing text.
Two zero bytes between the ending setup and the motion state.
Countdown reset to a random value from 20 through 51 by the update at $FB27.
Low three bits select the movement and pose handlers. The update copies them to $F73C before shifting the copy.
Three loaded zero bytes between the motion flags and their shifted copy.
Rotating copy of the flags from $F738, tested at $FB09 to call handlers for set bits.
Three split call addresses with high bytes at $F740. Code at $FB0E uses the bit index to patch its call at $FB1D.
High bytes of the three motion handler addresses. The low bytes start at $F73D.
Eight possible flag values selected by masking the random byte with seven when the motion delay expires.
Subtracts four from the split X coordinate. Sets rightward motion flags if the result is below $003C and selects frame $68 or $69 by the X position.
Adds four to the split X coordinate. If the high byte is nonzero and the low byte reaches $28, sets leftward motion flags. Selects frame $6C or $6D by the X position.
Incremented by the third motion handler, which uses its low bit to change the actor frame.
Sets sprite frame $2C on odd counter values.
Copies sixteen sprite frames from $F080 to $6440. Mirrors the frames at $6840 and $6800 to $6740 and $6780.
Copies X pages from the source pointer in $CA/$CB to $6440, advancing both pointers a page at a time.
Copies two pages from $F440 to $6440, then mirrors the first six 64-byte slots into $65C0–$673F. The mirror pass replaces the final two slots of the bulk copy.

Reverses both the three bytes of each of 21 rows and the order of pixel pairs within each byte. Uses the reversal table at $0600 and advances the source and destination pointers to the next 64-byte slots.
Forty split addresses with high bytes at $F8A6. The first nineteen entries point into the ending narrative. The final twenty-one point into the C64 credits at $C800.
High bytes of the 40 ending line pointers. $FA5D uses the same line index as the low-byte lookup from $F87E and the starting column lookup from $F8CE.
Starting screen column for each of the forty text row pointers, used by the self-modifying renderer at $FA69.
Zero-terminated screen-code text about Nakahama, followed by THE END and blank lines. The ending row pointers select the lines and their horizontal offsets.
Line 2 of the ending text. The renderer starts at screen column 8 and writes 26 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 3 of the ending text. The renderer starts at screen column 11 and writes 21 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 4 of the ending text. The renderer starts at screen column 9 and writes 23 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 5 of the ending text. The renderer starts at screen column 6 and writes 29 character codes before the zero terminator.
Blank ending text row, referenced by line 6 of the scroll list.
Line 7 of the ending text. The renderer starts at screen column 11 and writes 22 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 8 of the ending text. The renderer starts at screen column 10 and writes 24 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 9 of the ending text. The renderer starts at screen column 10 and writes 23 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 10 of the ending text. The renderer starts at screen column 8 and writes 28 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 11 of the ending text. The renderer starts at screen column 9 and writes 25 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 12 of the ending text. The renderer starts at screen column 10 and writes 22 character codes before the zero terminator.
Line 13 of the ending text. The renderer starts at screen column 15 and writes 12 character codes before the zero terminator.
Blank ending text row, referenced by line 14 of the scroll list.
Line 15 of the ending text. The renderer starts at screen column 17 and writes 7 character codes before the zero terminator.
Blank ending text row, referenced by line 16, 18 of the scroll list.
Blank ending text row, referenced by line 17, 19 of the scroll list.
Scroll position offset subtracted from the row index to choose which text line to fetch. Decremented when the scroller flips screens.

Clears the selected row on the offscreen page. On even row differences within the 40-entry table, patches its source address from $F87E/$F8A6 and copies a zero-terminated string at the table's column.
Indexed character load, patched from the split ending line directory.
Low byte of the current ending line source address. The loop writes characters to the selected row until the source byte is zero.
High byte of the string read operand at $FA69, patched from the line pointer table. The loop copies screen codes to the selected column until it reads zero.

Waits on $2B and redraws rows as the display shift in $2A advances. Flips screen pages every 32 steps and advances the text origin until $FA23 reaches $AE. Held fire lets intermediate steps run without waiting for $2B.
Initialised to zero in the ending path. The secondary sprite setup at $FC1B returns early while this byte is nonzero.

Handles a nonzero hit flag at $0C4E. Decrements the remaining count at $31 when $0C31 is clear and enters the ending when that count reaches zero. Otherwise dispatches motion by bits of $F738, selects random motion at delay expiry and chooses an in-air frame when $0C31 is set.
Calls the handler selected by the set bit currently being tested in the motion flags.
Low byte of the selected motion handler's call address, loaded from $F73D.
High byte of the selected motion handler's call address, loaded from $F740.

Immediate operand of the LDX at $FB20. The call saves the current handler index here and reloads it on return. After all three flag bits are processed, chooses new motion flags and a delay on expiry, selects the airborne pose and sometimes starts a jump.
Writes $F7 and zero to the two actor motion bytes and marks $0C31 active.
Low X bytes for eight recent actor positions.
High X bytes for the eight recent actor positions.
Eight recent actor Y coordinates. A zero entry suppresses the secondary sprite.
Recent primary sprite frame indices. The history reader adds eight to select the corresponding secondary frame.
Write index counter for the eight-slot actor history ring.
Offset added to the write index before masking the read index to three bits.
Two loaded bytes of value one after the history counters and immediately before the update code.

Copies an older position and frame from the eight-slot history into the secondary actor slot. Records the current pose when $0C31 is active and motion flag bit 2 is clear, or marks its history slot inactive otherwise. Advances the write counter and rotates the read offset by four.
Cycles the Y coordinate used by the secondary sprite initializer. Adds $2A and subtracts $50 for the saved seed when the new value reaches $6E.
When motion bit 2 is set and both $0C31 and $FAC6 are clear, picks a frame from $78–$7F, offsets the primary X by zero to seven pixels and selects Y using $FC1A.

The loaded tail begins with $0C, then encodes a store to $FC29 and code that wraps A by subtracting $50 when it is at least $6E. It follows the return at $FC6A. The preceding live routine has a branch to $FC6A, with $FC29 inside that branch instruction.
Zero fill after the alternate stage code through the mission number's preceding byte.
The one-based mission number used for this file and for play selection in the resident engine.
Four split pointers with their high bytes at $FCC5. The resident loader at $0B26 selects a stage and gives its grid to the row-pointer builder at $0B46.
High bytes for the tile grids. $0B2B takes the entry for the active stage and puts it in $FC before generating row pointers.
Four split pointers with high bytes at $FCCD. The grid parallels the tile map and the resident coordinate lookup at $3DFA masks each attribute to its low three bits.
High bytes for the attribute grids. $0B35 selects the high byte for $FE.
Stage widths used as a byte stride for the tile and attribute row pointers.
Stage heights used by the resident scaler to derive the vertical playfield limit and by $8EAD to walk the attribute grid.
Indexed stage values copied to $2D during setup by $0AFD.
VIC extended background register $D022 values selected by stage.
VIC extended background register $D023 values selected by stage.
Indexed initial view value written to $1781 before the character drawing loop at $1785.
Four split pointers with high bytes at $FCED. $8FE8 copies 128 bytes from the selected source into a separate workspace half for each player.
High bytes for the placement seeds. $8FF3 selects one for $FC before copying seeds to player workspace.
Indexed stage bytes cached at $0AEA and $0BE0 before display setup.
Stage index compared at $1A82. A match enables the alternate source at $D800 and installs the two operand bytes following this value at $1642/$1643.
Low and high bytes written to $1642/$1643 on the stage selected by $FCF5.
High byte of the stage-three callback address. The resident stage setup copies it into the call at $1641.
Four stage-indexed masks copied to $1901 at $0B11. The resident sprite routines AND their priority bits with this mask before writing VIC register $D01B.
The pair at $FCFC/$FCFD supplies the two operand bytes at $2B0A/$2B0B.
High byte of the pair installed at $2B0A/$2B0B.
Low and high bytes of the mission-provided routine that $1AB3 calls after preparing the stage grids.
High byte of the stage setup call target, installed at $1AB5.
Forty-eight loaded zero bytes between the stage hook directory and the shared bytes at $FD30.

A copy of the sixteen default C64 KERNAL RAM vectors at $0314–$0333. The entries begin with the IRQ, BRK and NMI targets $EA31, $FE66 and $FE47, followed by the BASIC and device I/O hooks. All five mission payloads carry the same copy.
Forty-eight loaded zero bytes between the shared bytes at $FD30 and the stage placement source at $FD80.

Stage 1 placement seed copied into player workspace by $8FE8. A record has a destination low byte, destination high byte and value. A zero value ends the loop that applies records to the working stage grid.
Stage 2 placement seed copied into page $0200. The resident setup applies the value of each record at its two-byte destination and stops at the first zero value.

Placement records shared by stages 3 and 4 in this mission, with an in-game destination word followed by a value byte. The loader supplies $70 bytes of this workspace source before the overlay ends at $FEEF.
